chunks: It is narrated from ʿAlī ibn Yaqṭīn, who said:

I said to Abū al-Ḥasan al-Awwal عليه السلام: A man died while zakat was due from him, and he instructed that the zakat be discharged on his behalf, but his children are needy. If they pay it, that would cause them severe harm.
So he عليه السلام said: "They should pay it out, then have it returned to themselves, and they should take some of it out so that it is given to others."

key_terms.أَوْصَى: he made a bequest or final instruction
key_terms.تُقْضَى: be discharged or fulfilled on his behalf
key_terms.زَكَاةٌ: zakat due as a financial religious obligation
key_terms.مَحَاوِيجُ: in need; poor and requiring assistance
key_terms.يُخْرِجُونَهَا: they should pay it out or disburse it

ai.seo_question: What should be done if a deceased person owed zakat and his needy children would suffer hardship by paying it?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning zakat owed by a deceased person whose heirs are themselves needy. Imam Abū al-Ḥasan al-Awwal عليه السلام instructs that the zakat should still be discharged, while allowing the needy heirs to receive from it, with a portion also given to others. It reflects the legal and social function of zakat in relieving poverty without neglecting the deceased's obligation.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1641 - It is narrated from Ali ibn Yaqtin, who said:

I said to Abu al-Hasan al-Awwal (Imam Musa ibn Jafar Al-Kadhim (as))
"A man died, and he had Zakat due on him. He instructed in his will that the Zakat be paid on his behalf, but his children are needy. Paying the Zakat would cause them severe hardship. What should they do?"
The Imam (as) replied: "They should pay the Zakat and then return it to themselves, keeping a portion to be given to others."
